name: Abraham Lincoln
info: Abraham Lincoln (1809–1865) was the 16th president of the United States, who led the Union through the American Civil War from 1861, issued the Emancipation Proclamation and was assassinated in Washington in 1865.

facts.born: February 12, 1809, in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky, near Hodgenville; second child of Thomas Lincoln and Nancy Hanks Lincoln, a frontier farming family
facts.died: April 15, 1865, at Petersen House in Washington, D.C., nine hours after being shot in the head by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre
facts.role: Member of the Illinois House of Representatives (four terms from 1834); U.S. representative from Illinois (1847–1849); lawyer; 16th president of the United States (1861–1865)
facts.known: leading the Union in the American Civil War; the Emancipation Proclamation of 1863; the Gettysburg Address; promoting the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery; the debates with Stephen A. Douglas in 1858; being the first U.S. president to be assassinated

t: Born in a log cabin in Kentucky and largely self-educated, Lincoln became a lawyer and Illinois legislator and returned to politics in 1854 to oppose the spread of slavery into the territories.

Elected in 1860 as the first Republican president, he took executive control of the Union's war against the seceded Confederate states, and on January 1, 1863, declared the slaves in the states in rebellion to be free.
He was shot five days after the Confederate surrender at Appomattox; later ages have honoured him as a martyr and the Great Emancipator, and some have disputed that title.
dyk: In 1849 Lincoln received a patent for a flotation device for moving riverboats in shallow water. It was never commercialized, but it made him the only president to hold a patent.
ev: Lincoln is born in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky
In his second campaign he wins a seat in the Illinois House of Representatives, where he serves four terms
He is elected to the U.S. House of Representatives as the only Whig in the Illinois delegation
He holds seven debates with Stephen A. Douglas in the Illinois Senate campaign; the legislature re-elects Douglas
He is elected the first Republican president with 39.8 percent of the vote in a four-way race, and South Carolina adopts an ordinance of secession
He issues the final Emancipation Proclamation on January 1 and delivers the Gettysburg Address on November 19
He is re-elected with 55.1 percent of the popular vote and 212 electoral votes to George B. McClellan's 21
John Wilkes Booth shoots him at Ford's Theatre on April 14, and he dies the next morning

sections.early:
Abraham Lincoln was born on February 12, 1809, in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky, and was raised on Sinking Spring Farm and Knob Creek Farm near Hodgenville. He was the second child of Thomas Lincoln and Nancy Hanks Lincoln. His father, a farmer, cabinetmaker and carpenter, bought several farms in Kentucky but could get clear title to none and lost hundreds of acres in legal disputes. In 1816 the family moved to Indiana, where land titles were more reliable. His parents belonged to a Separate Baptist church whose members largely opposed slavery.

On October 5, 1818, Nancy died of milk sickness. Thomas married Sarah Bush Johnston, a widow with three children, on December 2, 1819, and Abraham became close to his stepmother. Lincoln was largely self-educated: his schooling came from itinerant teachers and amounted to less than 12 months by the age of 15, but he was an avid reader. His father hired him out to neighbouring farmers and kept the money, as was the custom. A flatboat journey to New Orleans showed him slave markets that, according to the historian Michael Burlingame, "would leave an indelible impression on him".

In March 1830 the extended family moved to Illinois. Lincoln grew distant from his father, in part over Thomas's lack of interest in education, and later refused to attend his deathbed or funeral in 1851. From 1831 he made his home in New Salem, where he worked in a general store, served as a militia captain in the Black Hawk War without seeing combat, kept a store that went into debt, and was postmaster and county surveyor.
sections.rise:
Lincoln lost his first campaign for the Illinois House of Representatives in 1832 but won in 1834, as a supporter of the Whig leader Henry Clay, and served four terms. He read law on his own, was admitted to the Illinois bar on September 9, 1836, and moved to Springfield. In 1842 he married Mary Todd. Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1846, he spoke against the Mexican–American War and demanded in his "spot resolutions" that President James K. Polk name the spot where the war began, a stand that cost him support in his district. He had pledged to serve only one term and returned to his practice.

The Kansas–Nebraska Act of 1854, by which Senator Stephen A. Douglas let the voters of each territory decide the status of slavery, brought him back to politics. His Peoria Speech of October 1854 was one of an estimated 175 speeches he gave in the next six years on excluding slavery from the territories. He then lost a Senate election in the state legislature, joined the new Republican Party in 1856, and in 1858 accepted its Senate nomination with the House Divided Speech. His seven debates with Douglas drew thousands; the legislature re-elected Douglas, but the campaign gave Lincoln a national political presence.

His speech at Cooper Union on February 27, 1860, brought him into contention for the presidency. He won the Republican nomination on the third ballot in Chicago on May 18 and was elected on November 6, 1860, with 1,866,452 votes, or 39.8 percent, in a four-way race. No ballots were cast for him in 10 of the 15 Southern slave states.
sections.deeds:
Before Lincoln took office in March 1861, seven states had adopted ordinances of secession, and six of them declared themselves the Confederate States of America. On April 12, 1861, Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter. Lincoln called for 75,000 militiamen, and four more states seceded. He took executive control of the war: he imposed a naval blockade on Confederate ports, disbursed funds before appropriation by Congress and suspended habeas corpus. Dissatisfied with a succession of generals, he replaced George B. McClellan and then Ambrose Burnside, and after victories at Vicksburg and Chattanooga promoted Ulysses S. Grant to command all Union armies.

On September 22, 1862, after the Union victory at Antietam, he issued the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation, and on January 1, 1863, the final one, freeing the slaves in the ten states not then under Union control. Enlisting freedmen became official policy. At Gettysburg on November 19, 1863, he said that the nation was "conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal". He pressed Congress for a constitutional amendment outlawing slavery, which the House passed on January 31, 1865.

Under him Congress passed the first federal income tax in 1861, authorised paper "greenbacks" in 1862 and created national banks in 1863. The Homestead Act and the Morrill Land-Grant Colleges Act of 1862 and the Pacific Railway Acts supported settlement, agricultural colleges and the first transcontinental railroad. No foreign nation recognised the Confederacy.
sections.opponents:
Lincoln governed between factions. Copperheads, the anti-war Democrats, attacked his refusal to compromise on slavery and denounced the Emancipation Proclamation; Radical Republicans criticised him for moving too slowly to abolish slavery, and he pocket-vetoed their Wade–Davis Bill of 1864. In 1861 he supported the Corwin Amendment, which would have protected slavery in the states where it existed, and in August 1862 he wrote to Horace Greeley that his "paramount object" was "to save the Union, and is not either to save or to destroy slavery".

His use of war powers was contested. Chief Justice Roger Taney held in Ex parte Merryman that only Congress could suspend habeas corpus; Lincoln persisted. Under various suspensions 15,000 civilians were detained without trial, and several, including the anti-war Democrat Clement L. Vallandigham, were tried in military courts, which was condemned as an attack on free speech. After the Dakota War of 1862, in which hundreds of settlers were killed, a trial that the legal scholar Carol Chomsky called "a study in military injustice" sentenced 303 Dakota to death; Lincoln pardoned all but 39, and 38 were hanged in the largest mass execution in U.S. history.

Later critics have questioned the title of Great Emancipator. In 1968 Lerone Bennett Jr. called Lincoln a White supremacist, noting that he used ethnic slurs, opposed social equality and proposed that freed slaves voluntarily move to another country. Defenders cast his delays and racist rhetoric as concessions to political necessity.
sections.last:
Lincoln ran for re-election in 1864 under the label of the National Union Party, with the War Democrat Andrew Johnson as his running mate, against the former general McClellan. Grant's bloody stalemates damaged his prospects, and he wrote a confidential memorandum pledging to co-operate with the president-elect if he lost. Victories at Atlanta in September and in the Shenandoah Valley in October turned public opinion, and he won 55.1 percent of the popular vote and 212 electoral votes to McClellan's 21. On February 3, 1865, he met Confederate officials at Hampton Roads but refused to negotiate with the Confederacy as a coequal.

His second inaugural address, on March 4, 1865, closed with the words "With malice toward none; with charity for all". On April 9 Robert E. Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox. In his last public address, on April 11, Lincoln said that the vote should be given to some Black men, "the very intelligent" and "those who serve our cause as soldiers". John Wilkes Booth, an actor and Confederate spy who heard the speech, plotted to kill him.

On the evening of April 14 Lincoln and his wife attended the play Our American Cousin at Ford's Theatre. At 10:15 pm Booth entered the box and shot him in the back of the head. Carried across the street to Petersen House, Lincoln lay in a coma for nine hours and died at 7:22 am on April 15. Andrew Johnson was sworn in as president later that day. After lying in state, Lincoln's body travelled for two weeks by funeral train to Springfield, Illinois, where it was buried at Oak Ridge Cemetery.
sections.legacy:
The amendment Lincoln had promoted was ratified in December 1865 as the Thirteenth Amendment, abolishing slavery and involuntary servitude except as a punishment for crime. His assassination made him a national martyr, and abolitionists viewed him as a champion of human liberty. The sociologist Barry Schwartz states that his reputation grew slowly from the late 19th century until the Progressive Era, when he emerged as one of America's most venerated heroes, even among White Southerners; the high point came in 1922 with the dedication of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C.

Later ages claimed him in different ways. In the New Deal era liberals honoured him as an advocate of the common man; by the 1970s he had become a hero to political conservatives for his nationalism and his support for business. Schwartz argued in 2008 that his symbolic power has lost relevance since World War II. Frederick Douglass said that in his company "I was never reminded of my humble origin, or of my unpopular color". On Reconstruction, Eric Foner argues that Lincoln did not see it as an opportunity for a sweeping social revolution beyond emancipation, while Phillip S. Paludan suggests he was moving towards a more radical position on freedmen's rights.

In surveys of U.S. scholars since 1948 the top three presidents are generally Lincoln, George Washington and Franklin D. Roosevelt. He has been admired abroad by figures including Karl Marx, Giuseppe Garibaldi, Mahatma Gandhi and Nelson Mandela, who likened the "new birth of freedom" of the Gettysburg Address to the end of apartheid.

summary: Abraham Lincoln rose from a frontier childhood to the presidency in 1860 as an opponent of the spread of slavery. He led the Union through the Civil War, issued the Emancipation Proclamation and promoted the Thirteenth Amendment, while critics attacked his war powers and later his views on race. He was assassinated in April 1865.
